grf.observed_anchor: Current Clay Machine workspace already rejects readonly-memoryview-as-immutability and proposes snapshot/copy for mutable or unknown exporters until a lease/epoch contract is selected.
grf.generated_reality: An eager bytes copy at ingress is sufficient to make a mutable borrowed buffer provenance-stable.
grf.counter_reality: If the exporter can mutate concurrently while the copy is in progress, the resulting owned bytes can be an internally mixed state that never existed as one coherent producer epoch.
grf.falsifier: Copy a shared mutable byte buffer repeatedly while a separate process alternates the whole buffer between two uniform byte states; require every admitted copy to equal one complete producer state if copy-alone is coherent.

unusual_experiment.name: CONCURRENT_SHARED_BUFFER_SNAPSHOT_COHERENCE
unusual_experiment.environment: isolated local container; Python multiprocessing shared_memory; no VPS/self-hosted/production execution
unusual_experiment.writer: separate process alternated complete buffer between byte 0x41 and 0x42
unusual_experiment.rollback: shared memory unlinked; child process stopped; no persistent runtime mutation

implication.retained: Built-in immutable bytes may remain the strongest zero-copy reference substrate where identity/provenance are otherwise bound.
implication.rejected: Do not treat snapshot/copy from an actively mutable borrowed exporter as automatically coherent merely because the resulting object is immutable.
implication.required_contract: Canonical Clay Bytes/Buffer ingress must select and test at least one coherence mechanism for mutable concurrent exporters: producer quiescence, ownership transfer, immutable generation/epoch, lease/freeze handshake, or an equivalent mechanism that binds the copied bytes to one declared producer state.
implication.receipt_rule: If coherence cannot be proven, fail closed or classify the ingress as opaque/untrusted bytes with explicit uncertainty; do not mint provenance-stable semantic identity.
implication.media_impact: The same condition applies to image/video/audio buffers and high-rate streams; low-copy transport requires lifetime/epoch semantics rather than readonly-view flags alone.

candidate_pr_review.pr_741: Bytes/CLAYVM2 candidate snapshot_clay_bytes copies mutable bytearray/memoryview and is therefore directionally safer than borrowed views, but this experiment shows copy-alone needs a concurrent-exporter coherence contract before promotion as provenance-stable ingress.
